en.name: Pâté, poultry
en.summary: Poultry pâté — chicken or duck liver, whipped smooth or set in a terrine, often under a lid of clarified butter — keeps about 7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Leftovers should be wrapped in plastic film pressed against the cut surface. It is a ready-to-eat food and one of the more perishable things you will buy.
en.pantry: Poultry pâté has no room-temperature storage. A smooth liver parfait is barely more than liver, butter and cream — soft, wet, low in salt and acid, and blended, which spreads any surface bacteria all the way through. Serve it cold and put the rest back within the two-hour rule, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F). A terrine left out on a table through a long lunch has used up the safe part of its afternoon.
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and eat it within about 7 days. Press plastic film directly onto the cut surface every time so no air sits on it — poultry pâté greys from the face inwards faster than a coarse meat terrine does, because there is so much fat and so little structure. If yours is sealed under a cap of clarified butter, that cap is the seal, not decoration: cutting through it is the same as opening the product, the seven days start there, and re-melting butter over the top afterwards does not restore it. Keep it on a shelf rather than in the door, and well away from raw poultry.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for poultry pâté here, and none will be invented. Freezing is a poor idea in any case: a liver parfait is an emulsion held together by butter and cream, and freezing splits it, so it thaws grainy and weeping and no amount of beating brings it back. A coarse country-style terrine survives it a little better than a smooth mousse, but neither improves. Make or buy the amount you will finish in the week instead.
en.thawing: If it has been frozen, thaw it in the fridge, still wrapped, and eat it within a day or two. Never on the counter, and do not refreeze it.
spoilage: Grey or green spreading in from the cut surface rather than a thin skin you can scrape off.
A sour, metallic or ammonia smell instead of a rich, livery one.
Liquid or melted fat separating out, or a glossy slime on the surface.
Any mould, including under the butter cap.
tips: Press film onto the cut face every time; air is what greys it.
Serve a slice at a time and keep the rest of the terrine cold.
Write the date you cut the butter cap on the wrapper.
Buy small pots rather than one large one if you eat it slowly.

faq.q: How long does chicken liver pâté keep in the fridge?
faq.a: About 7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with film pressed onto the cut surface.

faq.q: Does the butter on top make pâté keep longer?
faq.a: Only while it is intact. The cap is the seal; once you cut through it the product counts as opened, and melting more butter over it does not undo that.

faq.q: Can you freeze chicken liver pâté?
faq.a: There is no timeline for it here, and freezing splits the emulsion — it thaws grainy and watery. Better to make what you will eat in the week.

zh.name: 禽肝抹醬
zh.summary: 禽類 pâté——雞肝或鴨肝打成細滑抹醬，或做成陶罐派，表面常封一層澄清奶油——放 4 °C 以下冷藏約 7 天。吃剩的要用保鮮膜緊貼切面包好。它是即食食品，也是你會買到的食物裡比較容易壞的一類。
zh.pantry: 禽肝醬沒有常溫保存。細滑的肝醬幾乎就是肝、奶油和鮮奶油——柔軟、含水、鹽分和酸度都低，而且經過均質攪打，等於把表面的菌散布到整體。請冰涼上桌，並在 2 小時原則內把剩下的收回冰箱，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。在餐桌上放過一整頓長午餐的陶罐派，已經把那個下午安全的部分用完了。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，約 7 天內吃完。每次都把保鮮膜直接壓在切面上，不要讓空氣停在上面——禽肝醬從切面往內變灰的速度比粗粒的鄉村派更快，因為它油脂多、結構少。如果你的產品封在一層澄清奶油底下，那層奶油是封口而不是裝飾：切穿它就等於開封，七天從那一刻算起，事後再融奶油蓋上去也還原不了。請放冰箱層架而不是門邊，並和生禽肉保持距離。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給禽肝醬的冷凍期限，本頁也不會憑空生一個。何況冷凍本來就不划算：肝醬是靠奶油與鮮奶油維持的乳化物，冷凍會把它打散，解凍後又沙又出水，怎麼攪都回不來。粗粒的鄉村陶罐派比細滑的慕斯稍微耐凍，但兩者都不會變好。與其如此，不如一次只做或只買這一週吃得完的量。
zh.thawing: 如果已經冷凍，請維持包裝放冷藏解凍，一兩天內吃完。不要放室溫，也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 灰色或綠色從切面往內擴散，而不只是表面一層可以刮掉的薄膜。
聞起來發酸、帶金屬味或氨味，而不是濃郁的肝香。
出現分離的水分或融出的油脂，或表面一層光亮的黏膜。
任何地方長霉，包括奶油封層底下。
tips: 每次都把保鮮膜壓在切面上；讓它變灰的就是空氣。
一次切一份上桌，陶罐其餘部分留在冰箱。
在包裝上寫下你切開奶油封層的日期。
吃得慢的話，買幾個小罐，不要買一大罐。

faq.q: 雞肝醬冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下約 7 天，並用保鮮膜緊貼切面。

faq.q: 上面那層奶油可以讓肝醬放更久嗎？
faq.a: 只有在它完整的時候。那層奶油就是封口；切穿之後產品即算已開封，再融奶油蓋回去也無法逆轉。
這裡沒有對應期限，而且冷凍會破壞乳化，解凍後又沙又出水。不如只做這一週吃得完的量。
